missionPremise: San Marcos parcels (48209:97650/97651/97652/97658, and 3 of 6 in a wider Hays sample) are served a fabricated buildableAreaSqFt/Pct: 0 ('no buildable area') from GET /api/spine/property-atoms/:id/facets, contradicting R-2 (_decisions/2026-09-11_ruling_b_reversed_polygon_only.md) which requires the buildable-area figure to stay refused until a verified atom backs it. Four sub-defects named: (1) publish-what-ruling-refuses, (2) the zero is probably geometrically wrong (nine-edge ring, five side-labelled), (3) hybrid payload wears one stale date, (4) 35,365 setback-corpus cells written with dateBasis:unreadable and no conflict row.
correctionToDispatchPremise: The dispatch's own PLAN-ROW header names repo: legacy-design-tools. This is FACTUALLY WRONG for defects 1 and 2, established with live evidence before any edit was made, not assumed: (a) legacy-design-tools' Express router has no /spine mount at all -- grep of routes/index.ts confirms every router mounts under recognized prefixes, and a comment in that same file states unmatched /api/* GETs fall through to the SPA catch-all (HTML), so LDT cannot physically be serving this JSON endpoint; (b) live-queried LDT's own real product surface (mcp__claude_ai_Smart_Site__get_smart_site, backed by LDT's brokerageNodeFacets.ts baked-snapshot route) for 48209:97658 and it correctly REFUSES the envelope (overlays[envelope] = {state:'refused', reason:'atom_path_pending'}, derivedFigures.denies includes 'buildable_area') -- LDT's own surface is honest and is not the bug; (c) traced the real composer to hauska-map's apps/property-explorer/api/_lib/atom-chain-to-facets.ts (adaptAtomChainToBakedFacets), confirmed via a vendored copy's own README in hauska-engine (packages/retrieval/src/serving-sweep/vendor/README.md) which names hauska-map commit d3510a6f as the verbatim origin of that exact file, and via that same file's own parsePropertyAtomsPath() function, whose comment literally reads 'Path shape after spine rewrite strip: property-atoms/:parcelNodeId/facets'. Flagged to the user mid-session (given the blast-radius of expanding into two more shared repos with ~100+ concurrent worktrees each); user explicitly authorized expanding scope to hauska-map (and hauska-engine for read-only investigation) under this same lane rather than standing down.

rootCauseDefect1And2.location: hauska-map apps/property-explorer/api/_lib/atom-chain-to-facets.ts, adaptAtomChainToBakedFacets() -- the 'no-buildable-area' and 'buildable' branches (~lines 2057-2138 pre-fix)
rootCauseDefect1And2.mechanism: Both branches serve buildableAreaSqFt/buildableAreaPct and, for no-buildable-area, a definitive status straight from the property atom's own outcome.kind/areaSqFt, with NO check for whether the underlying write-time geometry passed ground-truth verification. The composer already computes `depthWarm = isDepthWarmPromoted(c)` (true only when the atom carries a depth-warm promotion marker, i.e. passed hauska-engine's checkEnvelopeGroundTruth predicate -- P1 containment, P2 per-edge inset vs district setback, P3 front-on-street) but never gates the area/status serve on it.
rootCauseDefect1And2.whyThisIsWrong: _decisions/2026-09-11_not_specified_semantics_and_no_approximation_state.md Ruling 2: buildableAreaSqFt/buildableAreaPct are refused, not approximated, specifically because 'the only tested computation needs road-frontage edge labeling nobody has acquired' -- 'a shape-only approximation does not know which edge is front... a wrong answer about a specific parcel'. R-2 (ruling_b_reversed_polygon_only.md) independently requires the figure to 'stay refused ... until a buildable-envelope atom BACKS them', which this session reads as verified-backs, not any-shape-only-write-backs, given the MCP surface (LDT) implements exactly that stricter reading today and is demonstrably correct on live data.
rootCauseDefect1And2.liveGeometryEvidence: get_smart_site depth=node on 48209:97658 (live, 2026-09-15): boundaryEdgeFact.edges has 9 entries, roles [rear, side, side, side, side_corner, front, side_corner, side, side] -- 5 of 9 labelled 'side' for a real ~55x138ft near-rectangular lot. This is the exact shape the dispatch's own hypothesis names as able to collapse a long narrow lot to zero if every 'side'-labelled edge (including GIS-artifact vertices, not genuine separate side yards) is inset by the side setback. The atom carrying this parcel's buildable-envelope outcome has no depth-warm promotion marker -- i.e. it never passed the P2/P3 ground-truth check that would have caught a mislabeled inset.
rootCauseDefect1And2.decision: Fix by withholding the unverified figure (and the definitive zero status) rather than attempting to fix the write-time geometry computation itself. The exact inset/edge-labeling code that WROTE this atom lives further upstream in hauska-engine (packages/engine-core/src/geometry, depth-warm/warm-compute.ts, boundary-primitive/compute.ts) and reforming it is a substantially larger, higher-risk change than this dispatch's stated scope; 'refusal over fabrication' (Ruling 2's own stated position) is also the more conservative, more clearly-correct move given the customer-harm framing of this row ('the only open row where a customer can act on a wrong answer to their own detriment').

rootCauseDefect3.mechanism: applyEnvelopeSetbackOverride can fold a fresh parcel_record setback-axis override onto an atom-chain-derived envelope (the exact live disclosure text 'Reader-composed axis override (parcel_record) applied to one or more setback axes; other axes remain atom-chain-sourced.' is generated here, confirmed by grep -- it does not exist anywhere in legacy-design-tools, further confirming (a) above), but applyRecordPatch's returned payload never updated the top-level snapshotAt (or facets.bakedAt) to reflect that a newer read had been folded in. composeSetbackAxisScalar read each overridden cell's value but discarded its own `vintage` field entirely.
rootCauseDefect3.decision: Thread the axis cell's vintage through composeZoningSetbackOverride as a new setbackAxisOverrideVintage field, and have applyRecordPatch take the newer of the existing snapshotAt and that vintage -- 'carries the vintage of its newest axis', gated on an override having actually happened so an untouched payload never gains a bakedAt it didn't have.

defect4Disposition.finding: The 35,365 parcel_record_cell rows (San Marcos + 12 other Hays cities, per _inbox/2026-09-15_p200-hays-rails_close.json) come from a bulk, single-source classification writer (hauska-factory's factory-parcel-setback-cells job / parcel-setback-cells.mjs), which reads ONE setback-corpus row per jurisdiction keyed on zoningDistrict and writes it as a 'value' cell -- structurally distinct from legacy-design-tools' authoritativeSetbackSource.ts, which DOES already implement R-1's conflict mechanism (resolveMostCurrentSetback / a `conflict` field naming disagreeing candidates) for its own live atom-chain-vs-codified-table reconciliation.
defect4Disposition.openQuestion: The bulk writer has no second dated candidate to disagree with AT WRITE TIME, so 'conflict row' in the strict two-candidates-disagree sense the ruling's resolver implements does not obviously apply to these 35,365 rows in isolation. What is NOT established: whether these corpus-derived values silently diverge from whatever hauska-engine's own atom-chain independently computes for the SAME parcels (a genuine cross-system disagreement of exactly the kind the ruling exists to catch, just occurring between two systems -- the factory bulk writer and the atom-chain live-derive path -- that never reconcile with each other). Checking this at the 35,365-row scale requires direct queries against both hauska-factory's parcel_record_cell store and hauska-engine's retrieval-api/atom-chain store, which this session does not have credentials for and which a P-200 close explicitly warned against running ad hoc ('to avoid additional heavy-scan cost against a store').
defect4Disposition.plannedDisposition: Diagnose precisely and hand off as leave_behind rather than attempt a backfill write. A backfill into a production serving store is one of OPS-24's three explicit operator stop-points regardless of which repo it lands in; this is not a route-composer fix.
